references.text: Describes the same parts of the sacrificial animal (the fat, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the kidneys) that were to be offered as a peace offering to the Lord.
Repeats the instructions regarding which fatty parts are to be offered: the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
Aaron performs the same ritual with the fatty parts, the fat tail, the lobe of the liver, and the kidneys during his first priestly service.
Parallel text concerning the ram of ordination, including the fat, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the kidneys, and the right thigh.
The right thigh (shok hayamin) is given to the priest who performs the sacrificial service, which explains why Moses takes it here.
The same procedure for removing the fatty parts, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering.
